title: Adds a bump-based Marching Cubes option
abstract: # Summary - Our existing Marching Cubes functionality in quest only supports structured (Cartesian) grids, but we have users that want to run Marching Cubes on unstructured quad and hex meshes - This feature PR adds a `bump`-based Marching Cubes option to quest to run on structured and unstructured meshes - The algorithm is policy-based, and runs on cpu, omp, cuda and hip execution spaces - I left the original MC algorithm in place since it is currently more performant on structured grids - This is likely due to the new algorithm performing more work. Specifically: - it welds the vertices of the MC - it also generates a polygonal MC mesh, but our application requires a triangle mesh, so we currently triangulate the output polygons - We should instead have an option to use a triangle-based clipping table, which would avoid the extra work - Also improves the python script that generates Cartesian meshes as input to our MC example, and adds a new script to generate unstructured meshes for the MC example ## Benchmark performance Comparing the original ("native") Marching Cubes implementation against the new Bump-based MC on hip (rzadams) and cuda (rzvector), using "seq", "cuda" and "hip" execution policies. - Dataset: $960^3$ over $[0,2\pi]^3$ using gyroid scalar field at scale $(1,1,1)$. Marching cubes generates `8,933,625` triangles - Note that this is a **much** bigger dataset than we'd typically expect to extract - For reference, here's a screenshot (from VisIt) of a $256^3$ grid gyroid isosurface with about 630K triangles - For the timings below, we report inclusive and exclusive timings, as well as the percentage of the exclusive time on GPU, where appropriate - Seq entries have the form `inclusive (exclusive)`. - GPU entries have the form `inclusive (exclusive; %GPU)`. ### High-level summary | Method | rzadams Seq | rzadams HIP | rzvector Seq | rzvector CUDA | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Native MC | **9.09 s** | **5.26 s** | **8.63 s** | **146.59 ms** | | Bump MC | **17.98 s** | **821.35 ms** | **13.03 s** | **166.65 ms** | - Bump is around the same time as native for "cuda" - Bump "hip" is currently several times slower than bump "cuda", but much faster than native "hip" - The hip timings appear to account for allocation and initialization of large buffers, while the cuda ones don't. - (speculation) I suspect the latter are optimized away by nvcc but not by hip - Bump timings use an Umpire QuickPool with an initial 20GB allocation. - I didn't modify or try to optimized the native approach. - The expensive native hip runtime is almost definitely due to buffer allocation and initialization and could likely be improved - The Bump CPU times take about twice as long on the CPU as their native counterpart - A significant portion of the overhead is due to the welding, which is done in the bump algorithm, but not the native algorithm. ### Detailed native MC extraction | Annotation section | rzadams Seq | rzadams HIP | rzvector Seq | rzvector CUDA | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Total** | **9.09 s (24.28 ms)** | **5.26 s (22.78 ms;
